summary: Nerfstudio is the Apache-2.0 research framework that made radiance-field training approachable, and gsplat is the splat rasteriser that grew out of it and is now the busier of the two. They are scored as one subject because that is how people use them: gsplat provides the rendering kernels, Nerfstudio's splatfacto method provides the training loop, the data ingestion and the viewer. The pair reaches further into ordinary content pipelines than any other free tool here — it ingests captures from Polycam, KIRI Engine, Record3D, Spectacular AI, Metashape, RealityCapture, drone mapping and Aria glasses, it runs COLMAP itself when there are only photographs, and for radiance fields it exports textured meshes and point clouds, not just splats. Two facts a standards audience should hold together. The first is a split in liveness: gsplat has shipped through 2026, taking NVIDIA's 3DGUT, lidar rasterisation, new sensor models and NCore capture support, while the Nerfstudio repository's own main branch has had no commit since 29 July 2025 and its last tagged release is from November 2024, so the documentation a newcomer reads is older than the library it describes. The second is that everything here needs CUDA: this is the group's most capable free trainer and it cannot run on a phone, in a browser, or on any machine without an NVIDIA card. What it writes is a PLY, or a private directory of PNG images when compression is used, and its default world-space normalisation throws away real scale unless the operator turns it off.

coverage.note: gsplat is a rasteriser and little else: a differentiable splat pipeline with batch rendering, N-dimensional feature rendering, depth rendering, sparse gradients and multi-card distributed rasterisation. There is still no render graph or pass structure, and no place for triangle geometry beside the splats.
